faults.name: arp_reply_wrong_opcode
faults.why: replies go out with the request opcode

faults.name: arp_answers_any_address
faults.why: requests for other hosts' addresses are answered

faults.name: arp_round_robin_stuck
faults.why: a full cache always replaces the same slot

faults.name: arp_bad_frames_accepted
faults.why: frames that ended with tuser (bad FCS) are answered and learnt

faults.name: arp_no_holdoff
faults.why: repeated misses for one address send a request each time

faults.name: rx_ddr_nibbles_swapped
faults.why: at 1000 Mb/s the rising-edge nibble is taken as the upper half of the byte

faults.name: rx_nibble_alignment_ignores_sfd
faults.why: at 10/100 Mb/s bytes are aligned on the preamble instead of the SFD

faults.name: rgmii_rx_crc_skips_first_byte
faults.why: the FCS check is computed over one byte too few

faults.name: rgmii_rx_runt_not_flagged
faults.why: frames shorter than MIN_FRAME are not reported as runts

faults.name: rgmii_tx_short_ifg
faults.why: the inter-frame gap is one byte time short

faults.name: tx_no_padding
faults.why: short frames are sent without padding to MIN_DATA

faults.name: tx_underrun_not_poisoned
faults.why: a frame cut short by an AXI-Stream underrun leaves with a good FCS

faults.name: tx_10_100_nibbles_swapped
faults.why: at 10/100 Mb/s the upper nibble is sent first

faults.name: sf_commits_bad_frames
faults.why: the store-and-forward buffer passes frames with a bad FCS

faults.name: sf_keeps_fcs
faults.why: the store-and-forward output includes the FCS bytes

faults.name: filter_hash_wrong_bits
faults.why: the multicast hash takes the wrong six bits of the CRC

faults.name: filter_broadcast_always
faults.why: broadcast frames pass the filter with bcast_en off

faults.name: vlan_strip_leaves_tci
faults.why: stripping removes the TPID but leaves the TCI bytes in the frame

faults.name: pause_quanta_half
faults.why: a pause quantum is taken as 256 bit times instead of 512

faults.name: pause_not_honoured
faults.why: a received pause does not hold transmit frames back

faults.name: pause_frame_wrong_opcode
faults.why: the pause frame sent carries opcode 0x0002 instead of 0x0001

faults.name: control_frames_forwarded
faults.why: MAC control frames reach the store-and-forward output instead of being consumed

faults.name: stats_octets_without_fcs
faults.why: the good-octet counter leaves out the FCS

faults.name: stats_mcast_counts_broadcast
faults.why: broadcast frames are also counted as multicast

faults.name: jumbo_length_11_bits
faults.why: with jumbo frames the length counters stay 11 bits wide and saturate at 2047

faults.name: icmp_ttl_kept
faults.why: the reply keeps the request's TTL while its checksum assumes the new one

faults.name: icmp_checksum_not_updated
faults.why: the ICMP checksum is not updated for the type change

faults.name: icmp_answers_fragments
faults.why: a first fragment (MF set) is answered as if it were the whole request

faults.name: icmp_sum_over_padding
faults.why: the ICMP checksum is checked over the Ethernet padding too

faults.name: icmp_addresses_not_swapped
faults.why: the reply's IP source stays the requester's address

faults.name: igmp_no_router_alert
faults.why: the Router Alert option is missing from reports and leaves

faults.name: igmp_no_suppression
faults.why: another host's report does not cancel our pending report

faults.name: igmp_leave_always
faults.why: a leave is sent even when another host sent the last report

faults.name: igmp_timer_never_restarted
faults.why: a query with a shorter Max Response Time does not shorten a running timer

faults.name: igmp_ttl_two
faults.why: reports leave with TTL 2 instead of 1

faults.name: udp_rx_highest_port_wins
faults.why: when two port entries match, the highest index wins instead of the lowest

faults.name: udp_rx_no_pseudo_header_source
faults.why: the UDP checksum leaves half of the source address out of the pseudo-header

faults.name: udp_rx_padding_passed
faults.why: bytes after the datagram (Ethernet padding) are passed on as payload

faults.name: udp_rx_fragments_passed
faults.why: fragments are taken as whole datagrams

faults.name: udp_rx_options_not_skipped
faults.why: IP options are read as the UDP header

faults.name: udp_tx_zero_checksum_sent
faults.why: a computed checksum of 0 goes out as 0 (no checksum) instead of 0xFFFF

faults.name: udp_tx_ident_stuck
faults.why: every datagram carries the same IP identification

faults.name: udp_tx_length_plus_one
faults.why: the UDP length counts one byte too many

faults.name: udp_tx_long_payload_sent
faults.why: a payload one byte over MAX_PAYLOAD is sent cut short instead of dropped

faults.name: mdio_preamble_31_ones
faults.why: the preamble has 31 ones before the start bits

faults.name: mdio_turnaround_driven
faults.why: in a read the station drives the second turnaround bit that belongs to the PHY

faults.name: mdio_read_lsb_first
faults.why: the read value is assembled least significant bit first (clause 22 sends the most significant first)

faults.name: mdio_release_without_hold
faults.why: the line is released one clock after the last rising edge of MDC, short of the hold time at small DIV
